title: Capacity surge contingency budget and HC runbook
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a short-window contingency budget and headcount (HC) runbook for capacity surge events (unexpected demand spikes, model rollout retries, or regional outages that push traffic to higher-cost fallbacks). The goal is to capture near-term budget add-ons, prioritized HC flex levers, and pricing reaction sensitivity to protect margin and runway without immediate enterprise contract churn.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: finance managers, revenue ops, product leads (Hosted API), and platform on-call.
- Time horizon: 0–9 months (immediate contingency + 3/6/9 month phasing).
- Coverage: Hosted API variable-cost increases, Dedicated burst-topups, short-term contractor HC, and temporary price adjustments / credits.

Summary of key recommendations (top-of-doc):
1) Establish a $2.1M contingency reserve accessible by finance with an emergency draw workflow (CFO sign-off + CRO + Eng SRE ack). Reserve split: 55% capacity (cloud/GPU), 25% temporary HC (contractors/ops), 20% customer credits & marketing mitigations.
2) Pre-approved HC surge roster: 6 roles (2 infra SRE contractors, 1 capacity planner contractor, 1 billing ops contractor, 1 solutions engineer (temp), 1 data-ops lead) with an estimated blended cost of $62k/month.
3) Implement a 3-tier pricing reaction plan (soft-signal -> margin-preserve -> hard-rate-change) with automated thresholds tied to 7-day moving average cost-per-token above baseline.
4) Rapid telemetry to enable decisions: token-level cost, per-customer top-10 spend delta, and per-region capacity utilization (15 min window).

Assumptions and baseline unit economics (internal):
- Baseline hosted per-token cost (avg): $0.00037 per generated token (including infra, networking, amortized model cost).
- Target gross margin floor (hosted): 60% after cost of serving (variable).
- Baseline monthly hosted tokens: 2.4B tokens. Baseline hosted revenue: $0.0009 per token effective (net of discounts) -> ~$2.16M/month.
- Dedicated/Private contracts: largely fixed; only overflow to hosted increases variable consumption.

Headcount contingency roster (monthly incremental costs):
Role | Qty | Type | Monthly cost per FTE | Monthly total
SRE contractor (infra ops) | 2 | contractor | $22,000 | $44,000
Capacity planner (contractor) | 1 | contractor | $8,000 | $8,000
Billing ops (contractor) | 1 | contractor | $6,000 | $6,000
Solutions eng (temp) | 1 | fixed-term | $9,000 | $9,000
Data-ops lead (temp) | 1 | fixed-term | $5,000 | $5,000
-- blended monthly incremental HC cost: $72,000
(Assumption: contractors billed via vendor pass-through; benefits minimal; includes overlap for on-call ramp.)

Contingency budget allocation (initial $2.1M reserve):
- Capacity buffer (55%): $1,155,000
- HC surge pool (25%): $525,000
- Customer mitigation & credits (10%): $210,000
- Marketing / account-level mitigation (10%): $210,000
Note: The 10/10 split preserves runway for targeted rebates vs. broad credits.

Scenario modeling: 3 demand/cost scenarios (9-month view). Each scenario shows incremental monthly variable cost, draw from reserve, impact on gross margin, and recommended operational levers.
Scenarios: 
A) Short spike (2x tokens for 4 weeks, then returns to baseline)
- Incremental tokens: +2.4B over one month (double for single month).
- Incremental variable cost: 2.4B * $0.00037 = $888,000.
- Recommended draw: capacity buffer = cover 100% for month 1; use HC pool for urgent runbook support. Remaining reserve after event: $1,212,000.
- Pricing action: no immediate price increase; communicate to top-20 accounts and temporarily throttle heavy non-enterprise flows via QoS.

B) Sustained high tail (20% higher tokens for 6 months)
- Monthly incremental tokens: 480M tokens -> monthly incremental cost: 480M * $0.00037 = $177,600.
- 6-month incremental cost: $1,065,600.
- Reserve draw: capacity buffer covers 100% (1.155M) -> remaining reserve: ~$89,400.
- Margin impact: hosted gross margin falls ~8–10 percentage points if revenue per token unchanged.
- Recommended levers: immediate optimization sprint (caching, quantization advice via Optimize), targeted pricing uplift (soft-signal). Implement per-route batching increases and issue customer advisory.

C) Region-wide fallback + model premium (overflows to higher-cost fallbacks)
- Effective per-token cost rises 45% due to premium GPU and cross-region egress: new per-token cost = $0.000536.
- If tokens +30% for 3 months (due to retries): monthly tokens = 3.12B -> incremental cost vs baseline = (3.12B*$0.000536) - (2.4B*$0.00037) = $1,672,320 - $888,000 = $784,320 monthly incremental impact.
- 3-month total: ~$2.35M -> exceeds reserve.
- Recommended action: trigger Tier-2 response: initiate emergency pricing surcharge (see pricing ladder below), start sales outreach for enterprise rate-lock offers, adopt temporary request-level throttles for anonymous/free-tier, and activate cost-avoidance rules (route to cheaper model variants where acceptable).

Pricing reaction ladder (pre-approved):
Tier 0 – Soft signal (cost > baseline +5% on 7-day MA): Activate Optimize suggestions, notify customers, prioritize non-latency-critical batching. No price change.
Tier 1 – Margin-preserve (cost > baseline +12% or reserve <30%): Introduce temporary per-request surcharge for metered customers (3–7% markup) or tighten free-tier rate limits; sales-informed outreach for high-usage accounts explaining temporary measures and offering limited credits.
Tier 2 – Hard-rate-change (cost > baseline +30% or reserve exhausted): Institute temporary unit price increase for new signups and overage bands for existing customers (escalating 5–15% by band). All changes time-boxed to 90 days with review.

Runbook: escalation, approvals, and telemetry
- Telemetry triggers: 7-day MA cost-per-token, reserve burn-rate (7-day average), top-10 customer contribution to incremental tokens (rolling 14d), region oversubscription >85% of allocated GPUs for >3h.
- Approvals matrix: Tier 0 -> Engineering lead + Finance ops; Tier 1 -> CFO + CRO + Eng lead; Tier 2 -> CEO + CFO + Legal + Product. Changes recorded in Confluence with ticket reference.
- Communication templates: short email to top-20 customers, Slack template for #prod-ops, and public status page message. Attachments: recommended messaging (body examples included as Appendix).

Operational checklist (first 72 hrs):
1) Confirm telemetry and isolate cost drivers (model, region, customer).
2) Compute reserve draw estimate for 30/60/90 day windows and log in finance tracker.
3) Stand up cross-functional response channel (finance, eng, sRE, product, sales).
4) Deploy targeted throttles and cheaper-model routing for non-critical flows.
5) Issue customer outreach for top-10 incremental users.
6) Engage contracting ops for HC surge onboard.

Appendix: example short-run budgets (numbers rounded)
- Immediate-month cover example (spike): Capacity cost $888k + HC surge for 1 month $72k + credits/mitigation $50k -> immediate draw $1.01M.
- 3-month moderate tail: incremental cost $533k + HC $180k + mitigation $90k -> $803k/month average draw where applicable.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Governance: who signs for full reserve draw beyond $750k? (recommend CFO + CEO)
- Pricing optics: communications plan for temporary surcharge (legal/marketing review needed)
- Product control: implement per-route QoS toggles for free-tier flows as a permanent capability?

Next steps (owner and deadlines):
- Finance to create reserve ledger in PeopleSoft by 2026-06-05 (owner: Aisha).
- Eng/Infra to add 15-min window telemetry for per-region GPU utilization by 2026-06-10 (owner: Ethan).
- Revenue Ops to draft customer communications playbook by 2026-06-07 (owner: Maya).

Notes and provenance:
- Cost-per-token numbers sourced from internal cost model v1.9 (GH PR referenced above).
- HC blended rates use recent contractor quotes and internal recruiting rate cards.
- This is a working document; expect refinement after runbook tabletop exercises scheduled for 2026-06-14.

End of sheet.
